study.title: Real-time respiratory motion compensated roadmaps for hepatic arterial interventions

imaging.modality_detail: Nonsubtracted noncontrast and contrast-enhanced prenavigational X-ray sequences plus live fluoroscopy (in vivo porcine); mask subtraction used to extract vasculature for roadmap
imaging.frames_per_sequence: Prenavigational: median 163 noncontrast and 266 contrast-enhanced frames; marker sequences approx. 12 s

data_released.detail: Data available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request

task.task_description: Respiratory motion compensated roadmapping: patient-specific affine vessel motion model built from prenavigational free-breathing mask/fill sequences, respiratory state tracked from live fluoroscopy via diaphragm intensity centroid, combined with deep-learning guidewire/catheter segmentation for real-time compensated roadmap (CRD) or inverse compensated device (ICDD) displays.
task.clinical_application: Device navigation during hepatic arterial interventions (embolization, chemoembolization, radioembolization)

temporal_evidence.quote: is selected and registered to all remaining frames using an affine transformation

G2.quote: the study was performed using a normal porcine model with continuous ventilation, which does not perfectly replicate, but closely approximates, human hepatic arterial anatomy and respiratory motion

G3.quote: The purpose of the motion model is to establish a mapping function between respiratory state and vessel deformation.

G4.quote: Changes in the C-arm angulation would require repeating the initial scans to create a new 2D roadmap and recalculate the motion model.

G6.quote: most previous studies were evaluated through retrospective analysis of clinical or phantom images, while the proposed system was implemented in real-time and evaluated in prospective animal studies

other_limitations: Stiff microcatheters/guidewires deform vessels, not accounted for in motion model
Affine transform may not fully describe motion of smaller vessels
Cone-beam divergence effects with table movement not evaluated
Large changes in breathing type (abdominal vs chest) may cause motion estimation errors
future_work: Substitute more flexible motion models such as motion vector fields
Apply alternative respiratory signal extraction approaches
Combine ICDD and moving roadmap in side-by-side display
Verbal coaching to reduce large breathing changes during procedures
